correctness.rationale: PASS: Fourier inversion and renewal give q=1/G; integrating the dominant coordinate yields G=K(c)/sqrt(epsilon) times an expectation of (1-epsilon+epsilon*delta/2)^(-1/2). Since 0<delta<2 almost everywhere, its reciprocal proves the strict sharp sqrt(1-epsilon) <= qK/sqrt(epsilon) <=1. The logarithmic small-c cusp comes from integrating the quadratic transverse singularity and is uniform in epsilon because of this sandwich. ν_c concentrates at delta=0 for c->0, proving optimal lower factor. Symmetric convexity of K, and the 2D face coefficient via elliptical polar integration, are checked with their stated fixed-parameter limitations.
